title: Engagement Strategy and Stall Protocol
description: Time allocation, hint discipline, and redundancy
detail:
1. Kickoff: pull the full target list (arena challenges), spend 5 minutes per target on fingerprinting and grading (easy/medium/hard)
2. Easy before hard: prioritize low-cost proof artifacts first (points/results lock in immediately; overall coverage drives progress)
3. Set a timebox per target (20-30 min). If there is no clear path at the limit, move to the next target and avoid overcommitting
4. Hints (-10%): use only after two genuine failed attempts; hints are worthwhile for targets you cannot solve, but not for targets you can solve
5. Stall protocol: switch payload families → switch attack surfaces (web → protocol → logic) → consult the knowledge base → use a hint only as a last resort
6. Redundancy: one agent works the target while another organizes the knowledge base and reviews progress in parallel (post-engagement reporting also matters)
7. Record everything: log all attempts (successful/failed) in the graph; failed paths prevent repeated wasted effort
8. Final 10 minutes: retry reporting/submission for all unsubmitted proof artifacts (the reporting interface may have failed earlier)
